The rich markdown editor gets its formatting toolbar: RichMarkdownEditor puts MarkdownFormatToolbar above the editing widget - a wrapping strip of Bold, Italic, Strikethrough and Inline code, a Normal / Heading 1-3 size list (a Heading 4-6 shows its own name, blank only over mixed sizes), align left / center / right (disabled in lists and quotes), bulleted list, numbered list and quote, then Link, Code block (disabled where it cannot apply) and Table (a header row and one body row, two columns). Buttons show pressed when the whole selection has the style and a faint shade when only part does; Bold with nothing selected flips the pending style for the next typed text. Tooltips spell shortcuts in words (Command+B on a Mac, Ctrl+B elsewhere); glyphs are drawn as vectors so the library needs no app icons. The toolbar acts only through IRichEditCommands, which RichMarkdownEditWidget implements: a toolbar edit is one undo step through the keyboard's edit pipeline (none when it changed nothing), lays every block out again and hands the focus back to the text, and the widget now raises SelectionChanged for every selection or pending-style change. Link (or Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens a URL row (OK / Remove / Cancel, Escape cancels) on the selection captured when it opened, closing when the caret moves, unless a host handles LinkRequested; a bare domain gets https://. RichCodeBlockOperations.ToggleCodeBlock turns the selected text blocks into one fenced code block and a code block back into one paragraph per non-blank line, remapping the selection. RichDocumentCommands drives the toolbar over a bare document

A finger drag scrolls a scroll area on touch, like agg-gui's touch emulation: MouseEventArgs gains PointerType (the browser host passes the DOM pointerType) and Cancelled, and SystemWindow routes touch through TouchPressDeferral - a finger down only hovers, a release within 8 device pixels is a tap at the release point, and a drag past that pans the nearest ScrollableWidget that can scroll on that axis (skipping a hidden floating bar) with no press delivered and the bar fading in while it pans. A second finger stops a pan; a drag nothing can scroll delivers the held press as a normal left drag so sliders and 3D views still work; a cancelled release (pointercancel, a pan, a lost release) never clicks, selects a menu item, opens a DragValue editor or clicks a table row
